title: Felwood
body: Felwood was once the northern reach of Ashenvale, a serene forest beneath Mount Hyjal. In the Third War the dreadlord Tichondrius used the Skull of Gul'dan to poison it before the Legion marched on Hyjal, and nothing was spared: the trees blackened, the beasts went mad and the waters turned foul. Illidan Stormrage later took the skull and destroyed Tichondrius, yet the taint remained, and so did the demons. The Shadow Council plots from Jaedenar, satyrs defile the old ruins, and only the Timbermaw of all the furbolgs stayed pure.

title: Emerald Sanctuary
body: Hidden among the trees of southern Felwood, the Emerald Sanctuary is the camp of the Emerald Circle, a largely independent branch of the Cenarion Circle sworn to undo the corruption of this land. The tauren Greta Mosshoof directs the war on the Shadow Council, Eridan Bluewind strikes at the satyrs, and another druid searches for even a single pure source of water in the forest.

parts.body: There is none. The craters of Shatter Scar Vale still hold the fetid water that gathered in them when the infernals fell, and the search for one pure source in Felwood has failed.

title: Jaedenar
body: West of the road in central Felwood lies Jaedenar, raised on ancient night elf ruins and druidic barrow dens and named in worship of Kil'jaeden. It is the seat of the Shadow Council on Azeroth, and here the cult plots with the Burning Legion; one old barrow den has become the Shrine of the Deceiver. Below lies Shadow Hold, the cult's fortress, its depths hidden from scrying by four braziers named Pain, Malice, Hatred and Suffering.

parts.body: A night elf caged in the Hold came to Jaedenar with a Knight of the Silver Hand, Trey Lightforge, to see whether the Council was regaining its power. The cult tortured him to death, and his spirit was turned against her.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Jaedenar (built on night elf ruins and two barrow dens, named for Kil'jaeden, seat of the Shadow Council)

parts.body: A dreadlord, Lord Banehollow, keeps court in Shadow Hold, and his rival Hel'nurath of Xoroth plants spies among his servants to usurp him.

title: Ruins of Constellas
body: Northwest of the Emerald Sanctuary stand the Ruins of Constellas, once one of the many night elf settlements near Mount Hyjal. Its moonwell, long a symbol of renewal for the kaldorei, has been fouled with fel energy, and the Jadefire satyrs who hold the ruins use its waters to bring forth more of their kind. The Forsaken of Bloodvenom Post have taken an interest in that water too.

parts.body: The well serves a larger plan: its spoils pass north to the satyr Xavaric, master of the Jadefire at Jadefire Run.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Ruins_of_Constellas (one of many night elf settlements near Hyjal, moonwell corrupted with fel)

parts.body: A kitten released at the well came back a corrupted saber, obedient to its keeper, and the Forsaken apothecary who sent it is delighted: any means will serve to crush the Alliance.

title: Irontree Woods
body: Irontree Woods spreads across northern Felwood, once a peaceful glade, now roamed by crazed treants and warpwood elementals, some so far gone that the druids call them beyond any hope of cleansing. At the southern edge lie ruins where many treants once dwelt, and the ancients who protected this forest, whose bodies were destroyed when the Legion marched on Hyjal, are said to keep watch in spirit still.

parts.body: Xavaric's flute was carved from one of those ancient protectors, its spirit bound within by fel magic, suffering and never released.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Irontree_Woods (once a peaceful glade, crazed treants, ancients Hastat, Stoma, Vartrus)

parts.body: Freed, the spirit of the ancient Arei is led out of the cursed forest. As Ashenvale draws near its true strength returns, and at last it is at peace.

title: Timbermaw Hold
body: Timbermaw Hold is the home of the Timbermaw furbolgs, cut into the mountains of northern Felwood, and its tunnels are the road to Moonglade and Winterspring. While the forest outside rotted, the Timbermaw weathered the storm here, the only furbolg tribe to escape the corruption. They pay for it with suspicion: so many outsiders kill furbolgs on sight that the tribe trusts almost no one, and strangers are attacked within the hold.

parts.body: To friends who freed their kin of a demon's grip, the Timbermaw have sent an offering of peace for the leaders of their peoples.

title: Bloodvenom Post
body: Bloodvenom Post is the Horde's only foothold in Felwood, a small camp on the high cliffs above Darkshore beside the poisoned Bloodvenom River. Those who linger have their own purposes: a Forsaken apothecary experiments with corrupted moonwell water, a hunter looks beyond the hold to the secrets Winterspring's wildkin are said to guard, and an orc widow waits for vengeance on the furbolg overlord who took her husband.

title: Talonbranch Glade
body: Talonbranch Glade is a small night elf post in northern Felwood, south of Timbermaw Hold, built around a moonwell, and the Alliance's only refuge in the corrupted forest. Teachers keep the old disciplines alive here, and the druid Golhine the Hooded counsels that peace can be found anywhere by looking inward for balance, warning young druids that one day the Emerald Dream will call them to sleep for years.
